clue.text: It's used for drawing? That's crazy

definitions.meaning: a locomotive draws, that is pulls, a train; the short form of the word is the answer
slang for mad or crazy, from Spanish

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: short for locomotive, the engine that pulls carriages, and a slang adjective meaning mad.

clue.text: Purchase rising party has a say over

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for party reads upwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

indicators.note: over means the abbreviation is turned back

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Someone buys in at a party gathering momentum and gets a say over things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns REVEL into LEVER; 'over' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means a firm hold or grip that gives mechanical advantage, which leverage also means.

clue.text: Powerful passage in CP Snow?

parts.note: C P Snow wrote a novel whose title speaks of the hallways where power is exercised, so a powerful passage is one from his book title

explanation.walkthrough: C P Snow's 1964 novel is 'Corridors of Power', a phrase now used for the places where government decisions are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a passage, and C P Snow's novel spoke of corridors of power.

clue.text: Severe critic, one taking pledge with wife

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife
'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, who takes goods in pledge

explanation.surface: A harsh critic signs the pledge, perhaps of temperance, together with his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pledge' suggests a temperance vow, but here it is an item pawned. The pieces come in reverse clue order: the wife's word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch uncle is an idiom for a person who lectures or criticises sternly and frankly.

clue.text: Over the top, but it makes some exult rather!

indicators.note: some means part of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly gloats rather too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra means extreme, beyond what is usual, so over the top.

clue.text: Philosopher's follower links girl with painting in church

indicators.note: in means the painting goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
art means painting
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A man introduces a girl to the painting displayed in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Links' reads like golf links but is the joining verb: CARTE is linked with SIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cartesian is a follower of the philosopher René Descartes.

clue.text: Blameless course provider replaced Melba round fruit

parts.note: a uni (university) provides degree courses

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the fruit
replaced means the letters of Melba are rearranged

parts.note: a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A college caterer has replaced the Melba sauce poured round the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Peach Melba is a dessert, which makes the surface plausible; 'replaced' gives MABLE from the Melba letters, split by the fruit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeachable means beyond reproach or criticism, entirely blameless.

clue.text: Fellow Latvian producing blue pigment

parts.note: co-, as in co-worker, means a fellow or partner
a Balt is a native of a Baltic state such as Latvia

explanation.surface: A fellow from Latvia manufactures blue paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt blue is a deep blue pigment made from cobalt salts.

clue.text: Record Lake District artist put in package

indicators.note: put in means the district and artist go inside the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
the Lake District lies in the north-west, NW, of England
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter from the Lakes is included in a record package.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous area in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap is to wrap up or enclose, as one would package something.

clue.text: Minister returning books about second state

indicators.note: about means the minister and the books go around the next piece
returning means the minister's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend, a minister
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A clergyman brings back library books concerning a second matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does not mean 'concerning' here: the reversed minister and the books together wrap round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the states of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: It's like watching alumni at an Oliver production

parts.note: OBs are old boys, the alumni of a school

indicators.note: a production of something rearranges the words, so at an Oliver gets its letters remixed

explanation.surface: Former pupils attend a staging of the musical Oliver.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (old boy) is a British term for a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Observational means relating to observing, so like watching.

clue.text: Colourful display a trendy bachelor assembled in bank

indicators.note: assembled in means the earlier pieces are gathered inside the bank

parts.note: a bank of seats or keys is a row of them
in means fashionable, trendy
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree

explanation.surface: A fashionable single man puts on a colourful show beside a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a riverside, but it means a row, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc of spectrum colours in the sky, a colourful display.

clue.text: Bring back controls Louis XIV rejected?

parts.note: reins are the controls of a horse

indicators.note: rejected means the French word is turned back to front

parts.note: Louis XIV supposedly said 'L'état, c'est moi', I am the state, so he is l'état in French

explanation.surface: Asks whether the Sun King turned down a proposal to restore royal controls.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis XIV stands for French ÉTAT (state), from his famous 'L'état, c'est moi'; 'rejected' turns it into TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position, to bring them back.

clue.text: A US president's first dance

indicators.note: first means the president's name comes before the letter A

parts.note: James Polk was the eleventh US president

explanation.surface: A president's opening dance at the inauguration ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' reads as describing the dance, but it puts POLK ahead of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in duple time.

clue.text: Like study initially going into formation of archipelago

indicators.note: into means that letter is put inside the rearranged letters
a formation of something rearranges its parts, so archipelago's letters are rearranged
initially means take only the opening letter of going

explanation.surface: A study group sets off into a chain of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation of' rearranges ARCHIPELAGO and 'into' puts G, the first letter of 'going' ('initially'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographical means relating to geography, the study of the earth's surface, so it is like that study.

clue.text: Fish on southern river — it's plain

parts.note: a pike is a freshwater fish
the Taff is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: A fish caught on a river in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'plain as a pikestaff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes this staff a byword for something plain to see.

clue.text: Suitably covers British game in brusque manner

indicators.note: covers means the adverb surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: aptly means suitably
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A newspaper suitably covers a British game in a curt report.
explanation.definitionFit: Abruptly means in a sudden, curt manner, which brusque also describes.

clue.text: Bandy divorcee's new experience

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, such as a divorcee
a change is something new, as in 'a change is as good as a rest'

explanation.surface: A divorced partner enjoys a new experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandy' looks like the bowed-leg adjective, but it is the verb to bandy words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bandy words is to exchange them, as in an argument.

clue.text: Give up TV to play with this?

parts.note: to jack in is British slang for giving something up
the box is colloquial for television

explanation.surface: A suggestion to give up television and find a toy instead.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK IN is British slang for 'quit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a children's toy, a box from which a figure springs out, something to play with.

clue.text: Plain woman's afterthought about article

parts.note: Pam is a woman's name

indicators.note: about means the postscript goes around the article

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman adds an afterthought to an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are vast treeless grassy plains of South America.

clue.text: One way sibling goes about building restaurant

indicators.note: goes about suggests moving round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
bro is short for brother, a sibling

explanation.surface: A brother wanders around constructing a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes about' rearranges ISTBRO; 'building' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: Defence of one book involved in a libel? Not half

indicators.note: involved in means the two letters are put inside what follows
not half means only the first half of a libel's letters is kept

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lawyer's defence of a book caught up in a libel case is waved away with 'not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it keeps ALI, the first half of A LIBEL, and IB goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence plea that the accused was somewhere else when the crime happened.

clue.text: Confrontation with wise man supplying plant

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a brush is a brief encounter or skirmish, as in a brush with the law

explanation.surface: A clash with a wise man produces a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagebrush is an aromatic shrub of the North American west.

clue.text: Birds belonging to Italian city? No no!

indicators.note: the first No tells us to remove the second word, without it

parts.note: Genoese means belonging to Genoa, the Italian city
the word no, taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks if the birds come from an Italian city, and gets a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'No' means 'no ... in it': take NO out of GENOESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterbirds, the plural of goose.

clue.text: Bloomer made by sweet girl touring island?

parts.note: pet, like sweet, is an endearment for a loved one

indicators.note: touring means the girl's name goes round the next letter

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sweet young woman goes round an island in a bloomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like an error or a garment, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A petunia is a garden plant grown for its flowers, so a bloomer in the punning sense.

clue.text: Turn out with most of one's team

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word one, the possessive ending giving no letter

explanation.surface: A coach removes most of a player's team.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a football team based in Liverpool, England.

clue.text: One may have a difficult interview in store!

definitions.text: One may have a difficult interview in store!

parts.words: One may have a difficult interview in store!
parts.note: 'in store' seems to mean coming up in future, but it means in a shop, where a thief caught taking goods faces an awkward questioning

explanation.definitionFit: A shoplifter steals from a shop and, if caught, is questioned there by staff or police.

clue.text: Music-maker, one economical with the truth, say

indicators.note: say means the word sounds like the entry

parts.note: a liar is one economical with the truth

explanation.surface: A musician who stretches the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a stringed musical instrument of ancient Greece, a maker of music.
